description: Global seismicity of the last 30 days, read as remote GeoParquet by DuckDB. The map holds every event and its time slider narrows what is drawn; the summary and the table below follow that window through two dashboard variables rather than through the dashboard time range.

panels.description: Time range sync is set to `variables`, not `toMap`. Moving the dashboard range would re-run this query, and every event outside the new range would leave the browser — the histogram under the slider would rescale and the window could never be widened again from the map. Publishing the window to variables instead keeps the whole month loaded and costs only the panels that read them.

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SET force_download = true;

-- force_download is not tuning. This endpoint builds the parquet per request,
-- so each ranged read sees a different ETag and DuckDB aborts with "the remote
-- file has changed". One whole-file GET sidesteps it; at 378 KB that is free.
SELECT
  place,
  mag,
  depth_num               AS depth,
  event_time_utc_date_fmt AS time,
  latitude_num            AS latitude,
  longitude_num           AS longitude
FROM read_parquet('https://demo.getgeolens.com/api/datasets/2717becb-bfc5-4029-845f-24c3bbe19780/export?format=parquet')

panels.title: Sismicidad global — últimos 30 días

panels.description: Reads the map's window. Both variables start empty — before the slider has been touched — so each bound falls back to an infinity, and the summary covers everything rather than nothing.

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SET force_download = true;

SELECT
  count(*)                 AS "Sismos",
  round(max(mag), 1)       AS "Magnitud máxima",
  round(avg(depth_num), 1) AS "Profundidad media (km)"
FROM read_parquet('https://demo.getgeolens.com/api/datasets/2717becb-bfc5-4029-845f-24c3bbe19780/export?format=parquet')
WHERE event_time_utc_date_fmt
  BETWEEN COALESCE(try_cast($quakeFrom AS TIMESTAMPTZ), '-infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
      AND COALESCE(try_cast($quakeTo   AS TIMESTAMPTZ), 'infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)

panels.title: En la ventana del mapa

panels.description: The ten strongest events inside the map's window. Scrub the slider and this list follows.

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SET force_download = true;

SELECT
  strftime(event_time_utc_date_fmt, '%d %b %H:%M') AS "Fecha",
  place                                            AS "Lugar",
  mag                                              AS "Mag"
FROM read_parquet('https://demo.getgeolens.com/api/datasets/2717becb-bfc5-4029-845f-24c3bbe19780/export?format=parquet')
WHERE event_time_utc_date_fmt
  BETWEEN COALESCE(try_cast($quakeFrom AS TIMESTAMPTZ), '-infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
      AND COALESCE(try_cast($quakeTo   AS TIMESTAMPTZ), 'infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
ORDER BY mag DESC
LIMIT 10

panels.title: Los más fuertes de la ventana

panels.description: Deliberately unfiltered: this is the context the slider moves through, so it must show the whole month whatever the window is.

targets.rawSql:
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
SET force_download = true;

SELECT
  date_trunc('day', event_time_utc_date_fmt) AS time,
  count(*)           AS "Sismos",
  round(max(mag), 1) AS "Magnitud máxima"
FROM read_parquet('https://demo.getgeolens.com/api/datasets/2717becb-bfc5-4029-845f-24c3bbe19780/export?format=parquet')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
